memory_candidates.content: To make a shared surface (a registration hook, its verifier, and every per-repo slug-derivation call site) worktree-aware, resolve the checkout with ONE comparison: `git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir` from the same -C dir. Equal (including both failing, on a non-git path) means not a linked worktree -- behave exactly like a bare `--show-toplevel`. Unequal means linked worktree -- the common dir's PARENT directory is the checkout. `--git-common-dir` returns a relative path at a checkout root but an absolute path from inside a worktree, so absolutize before taking the parent. When the same resolution must be duplicated across several installed/stable-path scripts that cannot share a sourced library, bracket each copy in a begin/end marker-comment pair naming the lockstep obligation, and add a regression case that extracts the marker-delimited block from every copy and asserts byte-identity -- this converts a prose 'keep in lockstep' comment into a mechanically checked invariant.

When fixing a worktree-resolution bug for a repo whose own activation file (e.g. .claude-extensions.json) is TRACKED by git, a real `git worktree add` test will materialize that tracked file into the worktree's own working directory too, causing an existing 'CWD file wins' branch to short-circuit before the new checkout-resolution code path is ever exercised. To actually exercise the fix live, delete the worktree-local copy of that file after creating the worktree (a purely local, working-tree-only change that does not affect the checkout) to model the real target scenario (e.g. a throwaway CI/automation worktree whose checkout never tracked the activation file in the first place).
